clue.text: Make up crap about universal truth

indicators.note: about means going around, so one word wraps itself round the other pieces

parts.note: crap in the sense of dung, used as fertiliser
U is the film classification for universal
a truth is a fact

explanation.surface: Someone accuses a liar of inventing rubbish about a supposedly universal truth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crap' here is literal dung, the farmyard fertiliser, and it wraps around the two pieces that follow.
explanation.definitionFit: To manufacture a story is to invent or fabricate it, an idiomatic synonym for making it up.

clue.text: Eccles is upset over American leaving meat in case improper application results

indicators.note: upset means turned over, so in a down entry the letters run upward

parts.note: Eccles is the setter, so 'Eccles is' becomes I'M

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so the named letter drops out

parts.note: sausage is meat packed in a skin casing
A is an abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: The setter is upset because the American removed meat from a case, which is improper.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter naming himself means I or ME; 'over' just places MI above the rest in this down entry, and SAUSAGE loses its first A.
explanation.definitionFit: Misusage means using something wrongly, that is, an incorrect application of it.

clue.text: Religious female at school, reportedly, in West Midlands town

parts.note: a nun is a woman in a religious order

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so we go by sound rather than spelling

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: A nun attending a school in a Midlands town.
explanation.walkthrough: Say 'nun at Eton' quickly and it gives the town's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuneaton is a market town in Warwickshire, often grouped with the West Midlands region.

clue.text: Counterfeit pens left in bar

indicators.note: to pen something is to enclose it, as livestock in a pen

parts.note: counterfeit means fake
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Forged currency changes hands after being left in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pens' looks like writing implements but is a verb, to enclose. 'Bar' is a chocolate bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A Flake is a crumbly Cadbury chocolate bar, a well-known British confection.

clue.text: Man allowed to display garland

parts.note: a chap is a man
let means allowed

explanation.surface: A man is given permission to show off a floral wreath.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaplet is a wreath of flowers or leaves worn on the head.

clue.text: A French man carries Uniform? That's topical!

parts.note: un is French for a

indicators.note: to carry something is to hold it within, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a gent is a man
U is Uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A Frenchman in uniform makes a comment about current affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topical' suggests news, but in medicine a topical treatment is one applied to the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: An unguent is an ointment, a preparation applied externally to the body's surface.

clue.text: I lengthen changes in order to educate

indicators.note: changes signals that the letters are altered into a fresh order

parts.note: taken letter for letter as fodder

explanation.surface: A teacher stretches out the lessons to instruct the class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In order' sounds like an anagram hint, but the link is 'in order to'; the signal is 'changes'.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlighten someone is to give them knowledge and understanding, which is what instruction does.

clue.text: Head of oil drilling company gives expression of surprise

indicators.note: something drilling goes into the middle of the thing it bores through

parts.note: CO is the standard abbreviation for company

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, so only that letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of oil

explanation.surface: The boss of an oil-drilling firm makes a surprised remark.
explanation.walkthrough: The single letter bores into the company abbreviation: C(O)O. The surface also hints at a COO, a chief operating officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Coo is an exclamation of mild astonishment, chiefly British and informal, like 'gosh'.

clue.text: Start of computer game is second-rate

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, the only one taken

parts.note: the first letter of computer
rummy is a card game

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles that the opening of a video game is poor.
explanation.definitionFit: Crummy is informal for shoddy or inferior, the same as second-rate.

clue.text: Choice of brew with bubble rising

indicators.note: a bubble is round like the letter shaped as a ring, and rising moves it upward in this down entry

parts.note: a potion is a brewed drink

explanation.surface: A selection of brews, one with bubbles floating up.
explanation.walkthrough: The bubble is the O; in a down answer, letting it rise one place swaps it above the P, so POTION becomes OPTION.
explanation.definitionFit: An option is a choice, something one may select from alternatives.

clue.text: Devil's new advanced jolly personality

indicators.note: the letter standing for new is advanced, moved earlier, which reorders the word slightly

parts.note: Satan is the Devil

explanation.surface: An odd claim that the Devil's new, improved self is a cheery figure.
explanation.walkthrough: N (new) is the fifth letter of SATAN; move it forward two places and SATAN becomes SANTA. The 's stands for 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: Santa Claus is the archetypal jovial, ho-ho-ho character, so a jolly personality describes him.

clue.text: Hallucinogen obtained from fermented stale dung

indicators.note: fermenting churns and transforms a substance, so these letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: taken letter for letter as fodder

explanation.surface: A drug supposedly produced by letting old dung ferment.
explanation.definitionFit: Angel dust is the street name for PCP, a drug that causes hallucinations.

clue.text: Brew ale with subtle colour

indicators.note: to brew is to mix and steep ingredients, so these letters are stirred into another order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A brewing instruction: make a beer with a delicate colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Subtle' looks like an adjective qualifying colour, but it is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Slate-blue is a greyish blue shade, named after the stone, so it is a colour.

clue.text: Good boss makes soup with okra

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good
an umbo is the central boss of a shield

explanation.surface: A kindly employer cooks up a pot of okra soup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' suggests an employer, but here it is the raised knob in the middle of a shield, called an umbo.
explanation.definitionFit: Gumbo is a Louisiana stew-like soup traditionally thickened with okra, whose name it also takes.

clue.text: Ring Frenchwoman covered in dirt

indicators.note: being covered in something means being surrounded by it on all sides

parts.note: grot is British slang for dirt or rubbish
Mme, short for Madame, is the French title for a married woman

explanation.surface: A call to telephone a Frenchwoman who is caked in mud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like a phone call but is a noun. Grot is British slang for filth.
explanation.definitionFit: A grommet is a metal or rubber ring or eyelet that reinforces a hole.

clue.text: Hi, I'm Sarah Batty, religious sage

indicators.note: batty means crazy, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken letter for letter as fodder

explanation.surface: A woman named Sarah Batty introduces herself to a holy man.
explanation.walkthrough: Batty reads as Sarah's surname but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A maharishi is a Hindu spiritual teacher or guru, a wise man of religion.

clue.text: So long, and thanks again

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a casual British goodbye
second meaning: ta is informal British thanks, said twice

explanation.surface: A farewell with a repeated thank-you.
explanation.walkthrough: Ta is everyday British slang for thank you, so saying it twice is thanks again.
explanation.definitionFit: Ta-ta is a chatty British way of saying goodbye, and doubled ta reads literally as thanking twice.

clue.text: DIY ledge on bookcase with rockers hard to lower

indicators.note: the letter that abbreviates hard is lowered, moved further down this down entry, reordering the word

parts.note: a shelf is a ledge in a bookcase
ELP is Emerson, Lake & Palmer, the 1970s rock band

explanation.surface: Do-it-yourself instructions for a bookcase shelf, involving lowering things.
explanation.walkthrough: H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard; in a down entry, lowering it means moving it to the bottom of its word. ELP were a 1970s progressive rock trio.
explanation.definitionFit: DIY means doing it yourself, and self-help is relying on your own efforts rather than others'.

clue.text: Caught idiot with flower in Cardigan?

parts.note: an unusual abbreviation for caught; cricket's usual one is C
a nit is a fool
a flower is something that flows, a river, and the Wear is a river in north-east England

explanation.surface: An idiot is caught holding a flower in the Welsh town of Cardigan.
explanation.walkthrough: Cardigan is a Welsh town but also a garment; the question mark marks the definition by example. K for caught is unusual, perhaps borrowed from baseball scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardigan is a knitted jumper, so it is one example of knitted clothing.

clue.text: Conservative conned country

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
to be had is to be tricked, so had means conned

explanation.surface: A Tory politician has swindled a whole nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Chad is a landlocked nation in north-central Africa.

clue.text: Labour cleared broadcast

indicators.note: labour means work, and worked letters are reshaped into another order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A news item: the Labour Party has been cleared of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' looks like the party, but it is the signal; 'broadcast' is the definition, not the anagram cue.
explanation.definitionFit: To declare is to announce publicly, as broadcast means to make widely known.

clue.text: Light pollution finally stops after November

indicators.note: something that stops a gap plugs it, sitting inside it

parts.note: later as an adverb means after, subsequently

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of the preceding word, its closing letter alone

parts.note: the last letter of pollution
N is November in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Light pollution is said to end once November arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light pollution' reads as one phrase, but Light is the definition. 'After' is the adverb, meaning subsequently.
explanation.definitionFit: A lantern is a portable lamp in a protective case, so it is a source of light.

clue.text: Greek character hosts a dance

indicators.note: a host holds guests within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: lambda is a letter of the Greek alphabet
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Greek person throws a dance party.
explanation.definitionFit: The lambada is a sensual Brazilian partner dance popular in the late 1980s.

clue.text: Revolutionary stole coat, partly to get fur

indicators.note: revolutionary suggests turning round, so the letters run the other way
partly means only a portion of the words is used, sitting inside them

parts.note: read backwards, the run sits inside these two words

explanation.surface: A revolutionary stole a coat for its fur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stole' looks like the verb, but it is just part of the letter run.
explanation.definitionFit: Ocelot is the spotted pelt of a wild cat of the Americas, prized as fur.

clue.text: Marxist captures state capital

indicators.note: capturing something means holding it inside, so one piece is enclosed by the other

parts.note: Mao Zedong was the Marxist leader of Communist China
to put something is to state it, as in 'put it plainly'

explanation.surface: A Marxist seizes control of a nation's capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State capital' reads as one phrase; 'state' is the verb meaning express.
explanation.definitionFit: Maputo is the capital city of Mozambique.

clue.text: Preside over meeting daily, about one

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first word goes around the second

parts.note: a daily or char is a British term for a cleaning lady
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone takes charge of a daily meeting, around one o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily' looks like it describes the meeting; it is the old British word for a cleaner, a char.
explanation.definitionFit: To chair a meeting is to act as its presiding officer and run proceedings.

clue.text: I don't believe you become celibate?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a scornful phrase rejecting what someone has said
second meaning, playful: give up 'it', slang for sex

explanation.surface: A disbelieving retort to someone announcing they are giving up sex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' is slang for sex, so ceasing to be on it reads as becoming celibate; the question mark flags the whimsy.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a British idiom of incredulity, roughly 'stop pretending' or 'pull the other one'.

clue.text: Initially opposed unidentified Tory's extensive dalliances being made public knowledge

indicators.note: initially signals the opening letters of the following words

parts.note: the first letters of these five words

explanation.surface: A tabloid story: an anonymous Tory MP's many affairs are exposed.
explanation.definitionFit: To be outed is to have something private, such as an affair or one's sexuality, revealed publicly.

clue.text: Frenchman and Scotsman are in a state

parts.note: Louis is a typical French man's name
Ian is a typical Scottish name
A is the symbol for an are, a metric unit of area

explanation.surface: A Frenchman and a Scot are both in a flap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a state' reads as being agitated; the are is a hundred square metres, abbreviated A.
explanation.definitionFit: Louisiana is a US state on the Gulf of Mexico, named after Louis XIV.

clue.text: Those people initially establish unifying idea

parts.note: them refers to those people

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word after it

parts.note: the first letter of establish

explanation.surface: A group sets out the organising concept from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is the central subject running through a work and tying its parts together.

clue.text: Couple beginning to want closed borders

indicators.note: to border something is to sit on either side of it, enclosing it

parts.note: a door pushed to is shut, so to can mean closed

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, which is all that is taken

parts.note: the first letter of want

explanation.surface: A pair begins to want its frontiers sealed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Closed borders' reads as a political phrase, but 'closed' is TO, as in a door pulled to, and it borders the W.
explanation.definitionFit: A couple is a pair, and two is the number in a pair.

clue.text: Transparent form of calcite found in supermarkets

parts.note: Iceland is a British frozen-food supermarket chain
Spar is a chain of convenience stores and small supermarkets

explanation.surface: A mineral specimen allegedly stocked by grocery chains.
explanation.walkthrough: Iceland and Spar are both UK grocery chains, so the plural 'supermarkets' supplies two names.
explanation.definitionFit: Iceland spar is a clear variety of calcite, famous for showing double refraction.
